I watch the sunset paint the clouds like fractured ribbons of gold, drifting lazily off the horizon line where the sky gives way to endless white and nothingness. The waves crash down one by one with a wet, rhythmic thud that echoes through my ear as if they are singing a song I cannot quite understand at this moment's stillness. Then the tide rises, lifting the stones from the sand below like heavy boots on dry grass and pushing up into my chest, filling me up until I am almost entirely water and air. The salt water tastes of rain, salty and clean, brushing against my skin with a soft, wet kiss. I breathe in that fresh, crisp taste, smelling of the sea where the smell of the sea used to be. A gust brings the wind down hard upon me, rattling my hair and shattering glass. The waves crash violently again, sending foam dancing across the surface like a thousand tiny bubbles where the sun was shining before it set for good on those days I've had no moonlight in my eyes. I keep shifting in the water, trying to find balance between the wave and the shore, though I am lost in this endless dance of rising and falling within the vastness of the sea's embrace. The ocean is not just a body of water; it is an eternal conversation between sky and sea and everything that happens beneath them in silence or together with their sounds. It holds my breath while I catch the last drops of rain before the sun begins to rise again in a way that seems endless, like a star system where we are all just one point on a long line. I walk toward the shore, holding onto a rock that has been washed away by waves for years until it's completely flat and smooth now, waiting patiently for me to find my footing once more. The sea keeps watching us from every direction, silent and unblinking until we are all gone.
